basis: B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma is a blood-cell malignancy; the lymphoma designation also supports the immune mechanism axis.
Spastic paraplegia, auditory hearing loss and symptomatic hiatus hernia define SPG29; pes cavus occurs in 30-79%. Hyperbilirubinemia alone does not establish liver damage.
Bowed long bones and dysautonomia define the syndrome; corneal ulceration/scarring affects roughly a third or more. Respiratory distress alone does not establish lasting lung damage.
Primary ovarian endocrine failure with elevated gonadotropins and amenorrhea; this is gonadal hormone dysfunction, beyond isolated infertility.
Intermediate malignant teratoma is a germ-cell tumour, historically chiefly testicular; reproductive tumour origin has no axis, and no extragonadal site is specified.
Isolated developmental eye disease with microphthalmia, coloboma and sometimes cataract.
ID/seizures, congenital heart disease and hypothyroidism define the syndrome; skeletal abnormalities occur in 30-79%. Ocular abnormalities omitted because of the four-axis cap.
Asphyxiating thoracic restriction is defining; nephronophthisis/CKD and hepatic fibrosis affect substantial fractions (~30%+). Retinal disease is variable and omitted at the cap.
Proline-synthesis deficiency with cutis laxa and ID (22/23); osteopenia 10/11 and hip dislocation 15/22. Cataract 2/22; isolated glaucoma reports do not establish common eye damage.
Skin fragility and joint laxity define dEDS; hiatus hernia/reflux 80-99% and gingival disease support GI; myopia 3/4 and other ocular defects 30-79%. Bruising reflects tissue fragility.
Benign tumour arising in the parathyroid gland. Bone and renal complications belong to associated hyperparathyroidism and are not intrinsic tumour occupation.
Immune-mediated inflammation damages orbital tissues and extraocular muscles. Associated Graves thyroid disease is a separate disease.
Localized patellar articular-cartilage disease; the familial definition remains confined to the skeletal axis.
Tongue-palate fusion affects oral structures, micrognathia affects the jaw, and ear anomalies are explicitly defining. No evidence supports additional organs.
Cloverleaf craniosynostosis and thoracic skeletal dysplasia define the syndrome; the asphyxiating thoracic component entails restrictive respiratory dysfunction.
Immune-mediated inflammatory keratinizing dermatosis; hair and nail abnormalities share the skin axis. No common damaging extracutaneous involvement is established.
Arthropathy 80-99%, valvular disease 30-79%, hearing dysfunction 80-99% in supplied HPO; scleral/skin pigmentation alone is nondamaging; kidney stones are separately diagnosed.
Mandibulofacial dysostosis, bilateral hearing loss and learning disability define the syndrome. Cardiac lesions occur in 5-29%; a high palate alone does not establish GI dysfunction.
Macroglossia and omphalocele are defining GI anomalies. Neonatal hypoglycemia is usually transient; overgrowth/nephromegaly alone do not establish damage, and tumours are later risks.
Defined by vision-impairing corneal dystrophy and progressive spinocerebellar degeneration; both are core disease components.
Cortical atrophy and neurodevelopmental impairment define disease; myopic astigmatism, conductive hearing loss and ankle contracture each affect 1/2 assessed. Small denominators limit certainty.
Inherited cardiomyopathy with ventricular dilation, hypertrophy and sometimes noncompaction; no common extracardiac disease is established.
Corticospinal tract degeneration defines SPG3A. Weakness and amyotrophy are neurogenic; urinary symptoms do not establish urinary-organ damage, and skeletal deformity frequency is unspecified.
Congenital cardiac outflow-tract and ventricular septal malformation; no additional organ disease is specified.
Profound immune deficiency, agranulocytosis/marrow hypoplasia and defining sensorineural deafness (11/11). Liver disease and intestinal stenosis are single reports, not established as common.
